claim: The PR is a personal demo/test submission ('SNAP-demo', 'Automated PR from Termux') with no mathematical content the library needs: a stub operator 'algebra' ending in a sorry, a restatement of Nat.add_comm, and the author's own push script. Nothing in it is a candidate for Mathlib in any revised form.
requested_change: Close the PR. If the author wants to formalise something about operators on Hilbert spaces, discuss the goal on Zulip first and build on the existing ContinuousLinearMap / InnerProductSpace API in a personal project.
evidence: All three added files are covered by the findings below: each duplicates existing API or is not library material. The PR branch name in push_proofs.sh is 'feature/your-proofs', a template placeholder.

claim: Every definition in the file duplicates existing structure on H →L[ℝ] H. EndH is the type itself; id_op is 1; comp is *; O_k k is algebraMap ℝ _ k; S is -1; Ω O is O * O (O ^ 2); and the inductive predicate A, generated by scalars, -id, composition and squaring, is exactly membership in the range of algebraMap, i.e. in ⊥ : Subalgebra ℝ (H →L[ℝ] H).
requested_change: Drop the file. Use the existing Ring and Algebra instances on H →L[ℝ] H and Subalgebra / Algebra.adjoin rather than parallel definitions.
evidence: Mathlib/Topology/Algebra/Module/LinearMap.lean:936 `instance ring ... : Ring (M →L[R] M)`, :1137 `instance algebra : Algebra S (M →L[R] M)`, :351 `one_def : (1 : M₁ →L[R₁] M₁) = .id R₁ M₁`, :544 `mul_def : f * g = f.comp g`; Mathlib/Algebra/Algebra/Defs.lean:286 `algebraMap_eq_smul_one`; Mathlib/Algebra/Algebra/Subalgebra/Lattice.lean:233 `mem_bot : x ∈ ⊥ ↔ x ∈ Set.range (algebraMap R A)`.

claim: my_add_comm is Nat.add_comm (core Lean) restated, and its proof is literally `Nat.add_comm a b`. The general add_comm already covers ℕ through its AddCommMonoid instance. The file adds nothing else.
evidence: Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Defs.lean:200 `protected add_comm : ∀ a b : G, a + b = b + a`; Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Nat/Defs.lean:36 `add_comm := Nat.add_comm` in the ℕ instance.

claim: This is the author's local git/gh workflow, unrelated to the library. It regenerates MyNewProofs.lean, runs `git add .`, pushes to the author's fork and opens a PR with `gh pr create --head batmeezy918:feature/your-proofs`. It does not belong in the repository, least of all at the root; Mathlib's shell tooling lives in scripts/ and maintains the library.
evidence: Diff of push_proofs.sh (lines 15-24). Existing repository shell scripts sit under scripts/ (e.g. scripts/auto_commit.sh, scripts/lake-build-with-retry.sh); there is no root-level script of this kind.

claim: The PR bundles three unrelated things: an operator 'algebra' demo on Hilbert spaces, a Nat addition lemma, and a shell script for the author's git workflow. The title names only one of them ('Add SNAP-demo Lean file').
requested_change: Each item would have to stand alone. Given the findings on questions 1 and 2, none of them should be resubmitted as is.
evidence: Changed files: Mathlib/Algebra/MathlibDemo.lean, Mathlib/Algebra/MyNewProofs.lean, push_proofs.sh; title 'feat: Add SNAP-demo Lean file'.

claim: The one-line description ('Automated PR from Termux containing the MathlibDemo SNAP proof file') gives no motivation or design choice, never explains what 'SNAP' is, and does not match the diff: it and the title mention one file, but the PR adds three, including a shell script. It links no discussion. As a result a maintainer cannot tell what the PR is for.
requested_change: If anything is resubmitted: say what is being formalised and why Mathlib needs it, list every file the PR touches, and link the Zulip discussion.
evidence: pr.md description vs. the changed-files list. The script's own --title 'Add MyNewProofs' and --body text differ from the PR's actual title and body, so the PR was not even opened the way the script describes.

claim: The description does not say whether AI tools were used. The content looks generated: a physics-flavoured operator 'algebra' with ψ, a placeholder `def ψ_example : H := sorry -- user-defined state`, and template names such as 'feature/your-proofs'. Mathlib's contribution policy requires AI assistance to be disclosed.
requested_change: State explicitly whether, and how, AI tools were used to write the Lean code and the script.
evidence: Diff: MathlibDemo.lean lines 40-41 (ψ_example := sorry), push_proofs.sh ('feature/your-proofs'); nothing about tooling in pr.md apart from 'Termux'.

claim: The PR cannot pass CI as submitted. The new files are not added to Mathlib.lean, so the `lake exe mk_all --check` step fails. MathlibDemo.lean imports Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.LinearMap, which does not exist at the base commit. It leaves a sorry. Neither file has the `module` header and `public import` form that Mathlib files use at this base.
requested_change: Moot if the PR is closed. Any resubmission must be registered in Mathlib.lean (run `lake exe mk_all`), import only existing modules, contain no sorry, and follow the module/header conventions.
evidence: mlcount 'MathlibDemo|MyNewProofs' at base = 0 (not registered); .github/workflows/build_template.yml:410-416 runs `lake exe mk_all --check`; `mlshow Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/LinearMap.lean` reports that the path does not exist at 5160b96e; Mathlib.lean:1 `module`, :364 `public import Mathlib.Algebra.Group.Basic`; Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/Basic.lean:1-11 shows the copyright plus `module` header form.

claim: Material about operators on real Hilbert spaces is placed in Mathlib/Algebra/ under a 'Demo' filename. Continuous endomorphisms and their algebra structure live in Mathlib/Topology/Algebra/Module/, and Hilbert-space operator theory in Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/. Demonstration files do not belong in the library tree at all.
requested_change: Moot if the file is dropped (question 1). Otherwise put genuine results next to the existing operator API, and keep demos out of Mathlib/.
evidence: Mathlib/Topology/Algebra/Module/LinearMap.lean:936,1137 (Ring/Algebra on M →L[R] M); Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/Adjoint.lean:18-29 (operator theory on E →L[𝕜] E, including the C⋆-algebra structure).
